continuity: Begin from Episode 15 terminal water and inherited allocation agreements. Four delivered buckets stay with recipients. No unrecorded water gain or consumption.

verification: Match all 170 targets exactly once to a first-introduction episode; validation passed.

episodes.title: What the Storm Left
episodes.story: After the storm, Jon wants a quick all-clear so the community can resume daily life. An directs a ground-level inspection; the water protection holds, but the learning centre's roof and furniture need work. Jon stops treating speed as proof of competence. They agree to reopen the centre only after trained inspection and repair.
episodes.payoff: The protected supply is checked without inventing new water; the learning centre becomes the shared rebuilding objective.
episodes.voiceReason: Urgent inspection tests Jon’s impulse to rush.

episodes.title: The Test That Helps
episodes.story: Jon offers an overconfident demonstration at the temporary class. A teacher helps him turn a confusing exercise into a useful test of how people learn: simple physical models, translated labels, and a short illustrated story with a bear's paw and a wolf. episodes.payoff: Learners produce readable instructions for the centre; a practical lesson reveals the need for trained adult maintenance staff.
episodes.voiceReason: Jon’s awkward teaching attempt lets him question his own confidence; preserve his established age and personality.

episodes.title: Who Gets to Apply?
episodes.story: A community hiring notice offers paid maintenance and centre-support work. A new applicant from another settlement has useful experience but no prestigious qualification. A broken application terminal and a dismissive gatekeeper threaten to exclude them. Jon and Min insist on a paper alternative and a relevant practical assessment.
episodes.payoff: Applications are accepted fairly; the crew selection proceeds by demonstrated skills and clear duties.
episodes.voiceReason: An applicant faces exclusion under a deadline.

episodes.title: A Fair Trial
episodes.story: Candidates face a supervised practical interview. One assessor judges clothes and confidence instead of competence; another wants unpaid overtime to rush the opening. Min, sensitive about his own reputation, backs a fair skills test and written paid trial terms. The group rejects appearance-based selection and sets realistic staffing limits.
episodes.payoff: A qualified crew accepts transparent work terms; reopening now needs affordable supplies and a restored teaching garden.
episodes.voiceReason: Competing ideas of fairness and competence shape a consequential hiring decision.

episodes.title: Leave Room for the Bees
episodes.story: The crew clears the centre's neglected teaching garden. Jon mistakes a nest near the path for an enemy to remove. A knowledgeable gardener redirects the group before anyone rushes at it or strikes the insects. They cordon off the area and work on a safe section, learning why flowers and pollinators matter to the community.
episodes.payoff: A safe garden route and appropriate specialist care protect both people and pollinators; a local grower's donation supports the opening-day stall.
episodes.voiceReason: A mistaken intervention threatens the garden and calls for restraint.

episodes.title: What the Stall Is For
episodes.story: Min and a resident cook run a small food stall to fund approved centre supplies. Jon imagines a grand feast, then discovers that prices, portions and ordinary soup matter more. A customer challenges an exaggerated honey advertisement; the cook removes its weight-loss and calming claims. They choose a shared meal and transparent accounts over prestige.
episodes.payoff: The stall raises a documented supplies budget without changing the drinking-water inventory offscreen; preparations can continue.
episodes.voiceReason: Small practical mistakes and gentle self-directed humour expose Jon’s grand ideas about helping; no change to his age or identity.

episodes.title: A Promise Worth Believing
episodes.story: A confident vendor promises an instant repair and tries to sell a decorative upgrade as essential. Jon notices a clever use of true details to hide a false promise. A learner's question from a philosophy reading forces him to explain his reasoning plainly. The crew checks evidence, refuses the offer and uses the agreed budget for necessary materials.
episodes.payoff: The centre keeps its funds and completes the necessary repairs through the approved crew; inspection and the opening programme remain.
episodes.voiceReason: A persuasive offer tests the crew’s judgment and shared budget.

episodes.title: Who the Opening Is For
episodes.story: A newly introduced resident couple prepares an opening display of community photographs and memories. One partner hides from the camera, convinced that wrinkles and ageing make them unworthy of being seen. A younger adult worries about acne; Jon listens instead of offering easy reassurance. They choose photographs that show relationships and work, not idealized appearances.
episodes.payoff: The display honours real people across generations, including optional private memories of past losses without changing who survived.
episodes.voiceReason: Being seen and accepted matters more than outward appearance.

episodes.title: The Door Opens
episodes.story: Final inspection clears the centre for its agreed use. An enthusiastic young adult volunteer overwhelms the opening programme with their favourite music, while a neighbour worries that quieter visitors will be left out. Jon helps them make room for one another. The shared meal, garden route, learner writing and photographs become parts of one community event.
episodes.payoff: The centre opens with a named maintenance rota, consent-based responsibilities and continuity intact. Jon's role shifts from indispensable rescuer to one accountable member of the community.
episodes.voiceReason: People make room for different needs in a shared celebration.
